text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/chat/stream (p99 > 5s) across us-west-2. Triggered at 2026-03-14T08:20:34Z. Incident id INC-20260314-601. Auto-escalation to #eng-oncall.

Alice: ack, I'm on it. grabbing dashboard now.

Cheng: saw this in traces — tail tokens spiking, a lot of streaming stalls. p95 is ok-ish (~600ms) but p99 jumped to ~6.2s.

Maria: customer reports: chat streaming stalls and partial responses for long-context prompts (context > 8k). Impacting 3 paid tenants, one on Dedicated.

Alice: confirming: are we seeing increased cache evictions? last 10m eviction rate spiked ~3x.

Patrick: yep, KV-cache eviction count high on model-group:general-use-a. fragmentation metric also high. Looks like prefill pressure > decode throughput.

Cheng: exact anomaly: prefill requests are creating large KV segments (due to long prefixes) and decoder threads can't consume as fast -> cache churn and paging to disk. paging latency correlates with p99.

Maria: customer-impact status: P1 for the three tenants (partial streaming/stalls), majority of other traffic unaffected. Note: Dedicated tenant sees latency spikes despite isolated pool — likely cache fragmentation inside that pool.

Alice: immediate mitigations to try (suggested):
- disable prefill for long-context (>6k) on the hot model-group
- increase in-memory cache quota on affected hosts (temp)
- throttle non-prod/low-priority batch requests
- fallback-route: send new requests to model-variant b (smaller kv footprint)

Patrick: taking action: running command to flip prefill flag for group:
```
redwoodctl feature-toggle set --group general-use-a --prefill false --reason "incident: prefill->stalling"
```

DevOpsBot: Command accepted. Flag updated on 12/14 nodes. Propagation 30s.

Cheng: also bumping cache-reserve on the affected workers:
```
kubectl patch deployment inference-worker -n prod -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"worker","env":[{"name":"KV_CACHE_RESERVE","value":"0.65"}]}]}}}}'
```

Alice: good. throttle policy applied to low-priority queues (20% cap).

Patrick: routing rule applied: 10% traffic to model-variant-b, 90% to primary. Observing tail now.

Maria: FYI notified the three tenants via status page and direct email — included workaround: reduce request context length, avoid heavy prefill.

Cheng: metrics update 2m after mitigations: p99 down from 6.2s -> 2.1s, p95 steady ~580ms. Streaming stall rate dropped ~85%. eviction rate trending down but fragmentation still elevated.

Alice: good progress. Next steps: run planned rolling restart of cache service on the most fragmented hosts to defrag in-memory structures, schedule follow-up change to prefill rate-limiter. Want to hand off to Cheng for stabilization and postmortem.

Cheng: taking ownership for handoff. I’ll run rolling restarts one node at a time, monitor for page faults. Also opening an incident ticket and a postmortem doc.

DevOpsBot: Incident INC-20260314-601 updated: owner=Cheng, severity=P2 (customer-impacting).

Patrick: note: we should add a mitigation in Optimize: auto-detect prefill vs decode imbalance and temporarily pause prefill when decode lag > threshold. filed a PR here: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ops/issue/4387

Alice: thanks. handoff complete. Cheng, please include timeline, root cause (KV fragmentation + prefill imbalance -> paging), and long-term mitigations in postmortem. Will keep status page updated until stable. :thumbsup:

Cheng: will do. I'll post the postmortem draft in #incidents and ping for review.

Maria: glad we contained it fast. keeping customers updated.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260314-601 status: stabilizing -> monitoring. Last update 2026-03-14T08:24:40Z.
